title: Section 1
body_markdown:
SECTION 1
Passage 1
 Working from Home
1     As more and more professionals seek a better work-life balance and more companies adopt flexible policies to accommodate shifting workplace priorities, the working from home option is becoming increasingly viable. Employees see this as an ideal means to remain in the workforce and continue to be employed, thereby maintaining all the benefits of being part of an established company; while enjoying all the advantages of being based at home.                             5
2     By working from home, you save on many hidden costs associated with going to work such as costs of commuting car wear and tear; fuel, parking charges - and costs of maintaining and dry-cleaning an expensive professional wardrobe. Working from home offers the flexibility to determine your own work hours and work environment aspects such as lighting; temperature, and setting: It means you can basically work in the framework that suits you best and makes     10 
 you happiest and most productive. If you can choose your own work environment; you are able to determine a place with none of the unnecessary interruptions associated with the workplace; such as colleagues' teasing and unimportant meetings. Removed from the office stresses and distractions, professionals are often a lot happier and more productive.
3    The stress of commuting in bumper-to-bumper traffic at rush hour in many countries is   15 
 extremely counter-productive. It obviously leads to disgruntled workers who are already exhausted and worn out before they have even begun their day: This is especially true where the workplace is far from the office.
4    Often with long commutes, both physical and mental health are adversely affected: By working from home the commuting time saved enables you to resume physical exercise,  20 
 to go for a long walk for example before and after work or to join a local gym: Work and personal life balance, the aspiration of the modern professional, is often achieved and tuned to satisfaction through a working from home arrangement:
5    For many; the physical proximity to family and the convenience of being at home are tremendously comforting: For parents it can be especially comforting to know that they are      25 
 very near to their children and available should they be needed for any reason:
6    Working from home however; has its drawbacks. Often, professionals working from home complain of isolation and loneliness resulting from their removal from their bosses and co-workers: Since the workplace provides a location to meet people and make friends, professionals working from home have to be more creative and resourceful in getting to know   30 
 people and in staying in touch with their colleagues:
7    Although office distractions are avoided by working from home, different distractions may arise interruptions from children, neighbours, friends, family may be very disruptive and special efforts must be made to make it known that you are actually unavailable despite your physical presence at home. Added to these, is the difficulty in separating home from      35 
 professional work: The temptation to engage in household matters since you are at home is often very strong: Suddenly you may feel obliged to clean the home, do the shopping, the cooking; the home finances and the socializing all while meeting the full requirements of the job too. It is essential to draw the line between home and work so as to avoid both areas suffering:   40
8    Another disadvantage is that work does not really end: Since there is no-one looking over your shoulder enforcing strict hours, you may feel tempted to work endlessly.This pressure to
carry on working longer hours than you normally would may be compounded by the fact that you feel there are greater expectations made of you as a home-worker or by self-imposed pressures to prove yourself: Moreover; the lack of physical separation between home and     45 
 work may add to this pressure to work endlessly; not to mention the alienation from daily company developments: You may find yourself removed from important developments such as staff changes, new business, or changes in company direction. While working tirelessly in this self-imposed pressure, the danger of being overlooked for promotions and career development opportunities is quite real when you are away from the office. An open line of     50 
 communication with management and regular visits to the office are critical to prevent the out-of-sight-out-of-mind syndrome. Working from home is not for anyone: It takes a lot of discipline to motivate yourself to persevere in working at home without succumbing to the distractions and losing drive and momentum:

You think don't count for anything but you're wrong: Im just as important a citizen of this country as you are_ work every day building houses for rich punks like you: But you think that makes you better than me? "Well, it was the right thing to do.'

 Now" Jack jumped in and drove away: Michael hid in the nearby bushes while the two police cars raced by:

title: Section 1
body_markdown:
SECTION 1 
 Passage 1 Raising sheep
 Raising sheep can be a great option for farmers and others who do not have enough land to keep cattle but still want to raise some type of livestock. The general consensus amongst sheep farmers is that one can have four to six sheep per acre as opposed to one cOw and her calf per acre. Sheep are social creatures and are happiest in a group setting, so it is recommended that one keeps a minimum of four to five together: 5 2 Before starting any new pursuit; it is important to understand the costs involved. Fortunately; sheep can be relatively inexpensive to raise and the initial investment is loW: Start-up costs include the price of the sheep, fencing, and shelter. A farmer may even have the shelter and fencing already set up. On-going costs include any sheep feed required and health costs, including vaccinations and visits. Sheep are lovable creatures and raising them does not 10 require a lot of expensive machinery: A mower may be needed to cut overgrown fields, but proper pasture management should limit the need for this. Basic supplies will include a set of clippers for shearing, and hoof trimmers.
3
Sheep do not require complex or expensive shelter: They can survive most of the time outside provided there is some basic shelter from the wind and bad weather: Their housing can vary 15 depending on your budget and your climate. The ideal accommodation is dry; open-sided, and well ventilated: Hay; straw; or pine shavings used as bedding can provide extra warmth and comfort for the sheep. Focding shcop can bc quito affordable: pasture grass is the main gource of food for the sheep herd; but sometimes you may have to supplement this with sheep feed and other 20 grains: Proper grazing management will not only reduce costs associated with supplement feed, but it will also help manage overgrowth. It is important to keep a fresh supply of water accessible at all times  You should develop a timetable for rotating your sheep throughout your pastures because, if left too long in one location, sheep can wreak havoc on your fields: Overgrazing of pastures can kill the grasses, lead to soil erosion and increase farm costs 25 associated with re-seeding: Sheep eat a variety of forages including weeds and brush: This is very beneficial to a producer because sheep do not require high-quality forages. Sheep also eat grain that is lost in the field at harvest. They are versatile and can graze in various environments such as rugged mountain areas and on land where crops cannot be produced. Wool breeds can also withstand the colder regions of the country: Sheep can frequently 30 have multiple births and can be raised on a limited number of acres. They also yield many by-products that consumers use daily: Finally; sheep are produced for meat: 5 As with the production of any product there are always drawbacks Consumers are not willing to pay high prices for certain cuts of lamb, although less expensive cuts of lamb meat are available. The public's meat preferences are heavily drawn to beef and chicken: Another 35 adverse factor is that the meat processing and marketing structure fluctuates. This means that a sheep producer's enterprise may be profitable for one year but not the next; depending on how many sheep are marketed at a given time relative to consumer demand. Currently; there is not a high demand for wool clothing on the market: Unfortunately  sheep are easy prey for predators because they are unable to defend 40 themselves: They are also very susceptible to diseases, injury; and various external and internal parasites: Many of the parasites are deadly to sheep and can cost the producer a lot of money. Because sheep are fragile animals, producers must carefully manage them to prevent injuries. Another major issue is that labour costs for managing sheep are high and much of the work involved with sheep production is seasonal, such as at shearing and 45 lambing times ECoL 2018 0175/02/O/N/18

title: Section 2
body_markdown:
SECTION 2
 Passage 2
 The Mysterious Dream
The writer describes a mysterious dream that a teenage boy; Alex; has while at a boarding school. The dream almost leads him into danger:
Alex was lying in bed, the moonlight spilling onto his covers. He took a look at his watch: It was a quarter past two. He played again the dream he had just had: He thought about what he had heard; the boarding Master laughing and a clicking sound. That was strange. What had gone click? Had it actually been part of the dream? Suddenly, Alex was completely awake. He got out of bed, went to the door; and turned the handle. He was right He had not imagined the sound. While he was asleep, the door had been locked from the outside.
5
2
Something odd had happened, so Alex got dressed as quickly as possible and then knelt down to examine the lock: He could make out bolts, one at the top and the other at the bottom: They must have been activated automatically: One thing for sure, he was not going to get out through the door: That left the window; but all the bedroom windows were fastened with a 10 steel rod that allowed them to open 20 centimetres but no more. Alex was so determined to find out what was going on that he put his favourite Beethoven CD in the player and turned it on. As it started spinning at a fantastic speed, he held his breath as he thrust the edge of his CD against the steel rod. It took just a few seconds The CD cut through the steel rod like a pair of scissors through a paper: The rod fell away, allowing the window to swing fully open. 15
3
As it was snowing, Alex put on a sweater and a coat and then climbed out the window: He was two floors up. Normally a fall from that height would have broken an ankle or a leg but it had been snowing for the better part of ten hours and a white bank had built up against the wall right beneath him: He lowered himself as far as he could, then let go. He fell through the air and hit the snow; disappearing as far as the waist: Fortunately the bank had cushioned 20 him and muffled any sound that could have resulted from the fall. He was unhurt.
He climbed out of the snow and began to move around the side of the building, making for the front; He would just have to hope that the main entrance wasn't locked too. He had just made it t0 the side of the building when he heard the guards approaching, boots crunching: There was nowhere to hide, so he threw himself face down onto the snow; hugging the 25 shadows: He could hear the guards talking softly but he didn't dare look up. He held his breath, his heart pounding: They - walked past and rounded the corner: He was aware that he might not have much time, he had to move.
5
He lifted himself up and ran forward: His clothes were covered in snow; and more flakes were falling, drifting into his eyes. It was the coldest time of the night and, despite the short 30 stretch, Alex was already shivering uncontrollably as he stumbled towards the main door: He suddenly felt apprehensive. What would he do if it was locked after all?
Fortunately; the main door was unlocked: Alex pushed it open and slipped into the warmth and darkness of the main hall: The fireplace was in front of him: There had been a fire earlier in the evening and the burned-out logs were still smouldering in the hearth Alex held his 35 hands against the glow; trying to draw a little warmth into himself. Everything was silent: The empty corridors extended into the distance, illuminated by a few bulbs that had been left on. Only now did it occur to Alex that he could have been mistaken from the start: Perhaps he had jumped too quickly to the wrong conclusion and there was nothing mysterious going on at all: 40
